chapter_mission: Turn the theory into a workable plan, let the group touch Veraine's design directly, and set up the conversation with Kael that will decide the climax.
chapter_turn: The answer stops being abstract and becomes something built from specialized commitments.

scene_plan.purpose: Ben and Sera make the shared-burden idea concrete enough to test.
At the mast, let Sera read Veraine through her work and let Desh claim the sabotage role.
Ben approaches Kael without pressure and opens the only conversation that can finish the plan.

relationship_turns.from: conditional command (Ch14) → genuine request (Ch19) → earned trust (Ch21)
relationship_turns.to: true partners — Sera's handwriting on Ben's datapad, side by side. She may begin addressing him as 'Ben' once in this chapter, small, earned, not underlined

chosen commitment — Desh's volunteer move is his arc's new-truth moment. The former GAG operative choosing the dangerous task without being asked. The laugh Ben and Desh will share in Ch27 is purchased here

relationship_turns.from: earned respect (Ch10 stars scene, Ch19 outpost)
relationship_turns.to: invitation — Ben approaches with an ask that allows refusal. The hardest Skywalker move. Whether Ben has become someone different from his predecessors depends on whether he can mean it

expert recognition — Sera's read of the array component is the first time one of Veraine's peers has directly registered her material thinking. Per W2, this is evidence-of-passage beat 4 of five; the design signature carries the characterisation without requiring any spoken Veraine presence

exit_vector: First light on the ridgeline. Ben and Kael on the edge with the Scar below. Sera and Desh inside the camp, plans ready, waiting on the answer. Torin somewhere — not in this scene. Kael's question hanging in the air between them: why should I believe this one is different? Ben does not yet have the sentence that answers it.
notes: Keep this chapter tactile: notes, hardware, wind, ridge, hands on metal. Desh's volunteer matters because he gets there before anyone asks.
